ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a cyclohexane ring, and above the ring is connected an ester structure: the ring is connected to a carbonyl carbon, the carbonyl carbon forms a C=O double bond with the oxygen on the left and forms a single bond with the OR oxygen on the right; on the right there is also a separate H–OR component, and the figure has curved arrows and a negative-sign label, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows and excluding bonds involving hydrogen. Reasoning: Count non-hydrogen bonds by fragments: the cyclohexane ring has 6 C–C bonds within the ring; the connecting bond from the ring to the carbonyl carbon is 1; carbonyl C=O is counted as 1 bond; carbonyl C–O is 1; the O–R bond from the ester oxygen to R is 1; in the separate H–OR component, the H–O bond is excluded, but the O–R bond is counted as 1. The total is 6 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 11.

method.method_draft: Count bonds by fragments: cyclohexane ring = 6 non-H bonds; connection from ring to carbonyl carbon = 1; carbonyl C=O = 1; carbonyl C–O = 1; ester O–R = 1; in the separate H–OR component, exclude H–O but include O–R = 1. Sum 6+1+1+1+1+1 = 11.
